name: Welzl randomized minimum enclosing disk
definition: For randomly permuted P and boundary support R with |R|≤3, W(P,R)=W(P\{p},R) if that disk contains p; otherwise W(P,R)=W(P\{p},R∪{p}). Stop when P is empty or |R|=3, solving the constrained support disk base case.
variables: P remaining planar points; R constrained boundary support; p next point; W constrained enclosing disk
assumptions: Finite planar Euclidean points, uniform random permutation, robust containment and support construction; review degenerate and empty support cases before admission.
limitations: Expected linear arithmetic for fixed planar dimension under random order; recursive stack and worst-case complexity require separate review.
failure_conditions: Incorrect constrained support base case, invalid input or unreliable containment.
computation: Process a uniform random permutation recursively; only add a point to boundary support if the current disk does not contain it. Base cases and degeneracies must be independently reviewed.

source.citation: Provisional source locator: Emo Welzl (1991), Smallest enclosing disks (balls and ellipsoids), https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0038202 ; independent admission review pending.

name: Convex polygon fan binary point location
definition: For strictly convex CCW vertices v_0,...,v_(n−1), define orient(a,b,c)=(b−a)×(c−a). Reject points outside the extreme rays from v_0, handle those ray boundaries by segment containment, otherwise binary search for the largest i with orient(v_0,v_i,q)≥0 and test orient(v_i,v_(i+1),q)≥0.
variables: v_i ordered vertices; q query; orient signed cross product; i fan sector
assumptions: Strictly convex positive-area CCW polygon with n≥3; finite points, robust exact orientation and boundary handling.
limitations: O(log n) query after ordered polygon preparation; does not handle general concave polygons; boundary rays need explicit finite-segment checks.
failure_conditions: Invalid convexity, zero-length edges, unreliable orientation or unresolved boundary ties.
computation: Check extreme rays, locate angular sector by binary search, test the outer edge; include boundary points under closed-set membership.

source.citation: Provisional source locator: Algorithms for Competitive Programming, Check if point belongs to the convex polygon in O(log N), https://cp-algorithms.com/geometry/point-in-convex-polygon.html ; independent admission review pending.
